$generated.description: A marketing/landing testimonials block (social proof): an optional {it,en} heading (eyebrow?/title?/subtitle?) + an optional {it,en} ratingLabel template over a required non-empty items[], each { quote:{it,en}, author:{ name, role:{it,en} }, avatar?:{ src?, alt:{it,en} }, rating?:1..5 }; all text is {it,en} EXCEPT author.name, which is a plain (untranslated) string. It has a two-view: the wide view is a multi-column grid with every card visible, the narrow view a horizontal scroll-snap carousel whose overflow-x is confined to the track so the page never scrolls sideways. The optional 1..5 star rating is resolved from the owned `star` name-token internally (never raw code) with an accessible {it,en} label; the avatar is a structured { src?, alt } descriptor resolved to an when a src is declared, else the author's initials, never raw markup. No prop carries raw code.

a11y: Each rating renders exactly `rating` filled `star` glyphs that are DECORATIVE (aria-hidden), so the numeric rating is never conveyed by the star shape or its accent colour alone: the rating group carries an accessible name (role="img" + aria-label) templated from the {it,en} ratingLabel (or a component-internal {it,en} default) with the count interpolated (e.g. "5 su 5" / "5 out of 5"), so a screen reader announces the count as text and it flips with language, never a one-language literal.

The avatar is meaningful or marked: when a src is declared it is a real whose alt is the current language's {it,en} avatar.alt; when no src is declared no is emitted and the author's initials render inside a token-coloured circle marked aria-hidden (decorative, since the author's name is already visible text), so a screen reader is never confused by a bare two-letter glyph and never meets a broken/empty-src image.

The narrow view is a native overflow-x-auto scroll-snap carousel (no autoplay, no JS carousel state, no arrows/dots), so it is reachable and operable by keyboard and by scroll/swipe with NO focus trap and NO forced motion (prefers-reduced-motion respected); the overflow-x lives ONLY on the testimonial-track container so the PAGE never scrolls sideways, and any link inside a card keeps a visible focus-visible ring legible in both themes.

One <section> landmark hosts the whole surface as the AA-verified solid bg-background / text-foreground pairing; the quote is text-foreground, the author role / secondary text is text-muted-foreground, card borders are the hairline border-border, so axe A/AA (text and non-text contrast) is clean in BOTH themes on the wide multi-column grid AND on the narrow scroll-snap carousel. Both views render from the SAME items (one DOM, container-query class switch), so a screen reader / axe never double-counts the cards.
forbidden: No raw HTML/code or SVG string in any prop and no dangerouslySetInnerHTML: every text field (eyebrow, title, subtitle, ratingLabel, each quote, each author role, each avatar alt) is an {it,en} plain string and author.name is a plain string, so a declaration can never inject markup, a script, or an icon/graphic as a code or ReactNode slot.

The rating star is a name-token only: the `star` glyph is the owned iconNameSchema member resolved internally to a lucide component, NOT a prop, so a declaration cannot supply its own SVG/HTML/code string as the rating icon; there is no other prop through which a declaration supplies an icon or graphic.

The avatar accepts only a structured { src?, alt:{it,en} } descriptor (a URL string plus an {it,en} alt), never raw markup or a code string: an absent src falls back to the author's initials, never a broken , and the avatar can never carry injected HTML/SVG.

No hardcoded hue or hex/rgb/hsl/oklch literal and no arbitrary spacing/radius bracket: colour comes only from the accent-driven and semantic tokens (bg-background / text-foreground / text-muted-foreground / border-border / bg-card / bg-muted / --accent-ink / --acc-dim / --acc-line), and spacing/radius use only named scale steps (px-*/py-*/gap-*/size-*/basis-*/rounded-*), never a fixed value or a [13px]-style bracket; card and section dividers are the border-border hairline.

No autoplay / JS carousel / arrows / dots and no forced view: the two-view is a container-query structural change (a multi-column grid vs a native scroll-snap carousel), not a scripted slider, and a rating outside the integer range 1..5 (0, 6, or a non-integer such as 2.5) is a contract error (InvalidComponentPropsError), never clamped and rendered.
